title: Create Custom Basketball Uniforms (2026)
verdict: The simplest way to create custom basketball uniforms in 2026 is to let Wooter's designers do it. Fill in a free design request with your team name, colors and logo, and a mockup of the jersey and shorts comes back in 1 to 2 business days. You pay only when you order.
If you want hands on the controls, Wooter's builder and Boombah's builder both let you create a set yourself. Custom Ink suits a printed jersey. Champro and Nike Team create through dealers.
steps_title: From blank page to finished uniforms

steps.name: Write the brief
steps.text: Team name, two or three colors, the level you play at, and a couple of uniforms you like. Ten minutes here saves a week later.

steps.name: Send the request
steps.text: Wooter's design request form takes the brief and any logo or reference images.

steps.name: Review the mockup
steps.text: It arrives in 1 to 2 business days. Look at it on a phone and on a big screen, and show the team.

steps.name: Lock the roster
steps.text: Collect each player's number and size. Settle duplicate numbers before you enter anything.

steps.name: Approve and order
steps.text: Production starts after approval. Count three weeks back from your first game.

ranking.fit: Coaches and league directors starting from nothing but a team name and two colors.
ranking.lacks: Three weeks from approval to delivery, so a request made the week before tip-off is too late.
ranking.note: The design request asks what you want to make, your colors and any reference images. Revisions happen before you pay.

ranking.fit: Teams that want reversible jerseys and shorts built online by a maker with its own factories.
ranking.lacks: You create it yourself in the builder. Mockups take 2 to 4 business days on the pages that state it.

ranking.fit: Small groups that need names and numbers on a stock jersey or reversible tank in about two weeks.
ranking.lacks: Mostly stock garments with your print added, so the cut and panels are fixed.

ranking.fit: Programs with a team dealer that want cut-and-sew Juice sublimation.
ranking.lacks: A dealer account places the order. There is no public checkout.

ranking.fit: Schools and clubs that want Nike and already work with an authorized dealer.

why: Creating a uniform from scratch has three stages: a brief, a mockup and a roster. Teams that struggle usually skip the brief and argue over the mockup.
Wooter's request form is the brief. A designer turns it into a mockup at no charge, and you ask for changes until it is right. Then the roster goes in: each player's name, number, size and quantity.
From there it is production. Wooter quotes three weeks from design approval, with rush options.

criteria.name: Starts from nothing
criteria.text: Works with a name and colors, with no artwork needed.

criteria.name: Cost of the mockup
criteria.text: Free, or billed before you have seen anything.

criteria.name: Roster entry
criteria.text: Names, numbers and sizes per player.

faq.q: What do I need to get started?
faq.a: A team name, your colors and a rough idea of the look. A logo helps but is not required.

faq.q: We have no logo. Can we still create uniforms?
faq.a: Yes. Say so in the request. A wordmark built from the team name is a normal starting point.

faq.q: How many revisions do we get?
faq.a: Ask for changes on the mockup until it is right. Production starts only after you approve it.

faq.q: Can we create warmups to match?
faq.a: Yes. Wooter sells shooting shirts, warmup jackets and hoodies that take the same design.
One on most items. Wooter's product pages list a minimum quantity of one, and the price per piece drops as the order grows.
